question: Why is getting the family involved crucial for successful home health care?

options.A: Families are legally required to pay for all hospital expenses
options.B: Families replace the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: Family members make all final medical diagnoses
options.D: Family members perform many daily care tasks between professional visits

explanation: Informal caregivers handle routines like feeding and giving medication reminders when you're not there. Partnering with them makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h6)

question: What makes evacuating a sick patient off a ship so tricky and dangerous?

options.A: Excessive paperwork required by land-based police
options.B: The legal prohibition of helicopters over international waters
options.C: Adverse weather and difficult transfer conditions at sea
options.D: Lack of any communication tools between ship and shore

explanation: Spot on! Shifting waves and high winds make moving a patient via helicopter hoist or between two moving boats extremely risky. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T15#GNS321_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the main job of amniotic fluid during pregnancy?

options.A: Filtering metabolic wastes directly out of maternal blood
options.B: Preventing the mixing of maternal and foetal red blood cells
options.C: Protecting against physical trauma and allowing movement
options.D: Supplying all essential maternal hormones to the placenta

explanation: Spot on! Amniotic fluid acts like a safe cushion against bumps, keeps the baby warm, and lets them stretch and move their limbs freely. You're building solid clinical knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h4)

question: A nurse uses a video call to inspect a healing surgical wound for an elderly patient at home. Which model of care does this represent?

options.A: Inpatient intensive care model
options.B: Home care nursing model
options.C: Pure administrative billing model
options.D: Emergency trauma surgery model

explanation: Using video visits to monitor recovery and wound healing at home falls under the home care tele-nursing model. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h3)

question: What happens when a nurse falls into 'confirmation bias' during clinical assessment?

options.A: Forgetting to check vital signs because of a sudden emergency
options.B: Trusting equipment alarms even when they are making false noises
options.C: Blaming a coworker for a mistake you made during a procedure
options.D: Looking only for signs that prove your first guess and ignoring others

explanation: You got it! Confirmation bias is when our brain only looks for clues that match our very first thought about what is wrong, while ignoring other important signs. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h2)

question: Why is closely monitoring urine output so crucial for a patient with sepsis?

options.A: It proves that the patient is drinking enough oral fluids
options.B: It is a reliable indicator of adequate kidney perfusion and fluid status
options.C: It prevents the bladder from becoming distended during sleep
options.D: It eliminates the need to check blood pressure every hour

explanation: Urine output is our window into how well the kidneys and vital organs are getting blood flow. Good urine output means the body is holding up against shock! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h7)

question: Who takes ultimate responsibility for the surgical procedure?

options.A: The scrub nurse
options.B: The circulating nurse
options.C: The anaesthetist
options.D: The surgeon

explanation: The surgeon leads the team and carries the main legal and clinical responsibility for how the surgery goes. Every team member has a vital role, but the lead surgeon guides the ship! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h2)

question: What are the three core ingredients needed for valid informed consent?

options.A: Payment of all hospital bills in advance
options.B: Written signature from the village head and husband
options.C: Voluntary agreement, full information, and mental capacity
options.D: Verbal agreement witnessed by two police officers

explanation: For consent to be valid, the patient must agree freely, understand the risks and benefits, and be mentally capable of making the choice. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: How should the scrub nurse and circulating nurse perform the swab counts?

options.A: By guessing the total based on how many packets opened
options.B: Out loud together in a synchronized manner
options.C: Silently by themselves to avoid disturbing the surgeon
options.D: Independently without comparing their numbers

explanation: Always count out loud together! It keeps everyone on the same page and prevents nasty miscount surprises. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: When does the problem-solving process officially reach its completion?

options.A: When the nurse finishes charting at the end of the shift
options.B: Before the nurse begins the physical assessment of the patient
options.C: As soon as the doctor writes the medication order
options.D: After evaluating whether the chosen intervention met the patient's goals

explanation: Evaluation is the final step that determines if the problem was actually solved by the action taken. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which human cell receptors does SARS-CoV-2 mainly latch onto?

options.A: Cholinergic receptors
options.B: Insulin receptors
options.C: ACE2 receptors
options.D: Beta-adrenergic receptors

explanation: ACE2 receptors are found in large amounts in our lung tissue, making them the main doorway for the virus to enter the body. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which common virus is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of HPV can cause changes in cervical cells over time. This is why screening and the HPV vaccine are such big wins in public health! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h3)

question: What symptom should a pregnant woman be taught is a red flag requiring immediate contact with her clinic?

options.A: Inability to keep any fluids down for twenty-four hours
options.B: A slight increase in appetite during the second trimester
options.C: Occasional mild bloating after eating plain toast
options.D: Mild tiredness during the middle of the afternoon

explanation: Not being able to retain any fluids for a full day puts the mother at high risk for dangerous dehydration. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h7)

question: How does social justice guide a community health nurse during advocacy?

options.A: It drives the nurse to fight for fair access to health resources for everyone
options.B: It requires the nurse to obey hospital management without question
options.C: It forces the nurse to prioritize wealthy patients who pay higher taxes
options.D: It allows the nurse to make medical diagnoses independently

explanation: Well done! Social justice is about fairness—making sure everyone, rich or poor, gets a fair share of healthcare resources to close health gaps. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h2)

question: What essential details should you include in your nursing notes after an ear exam?

options.A: A detailed diagram of the patient's skull bones and cranial nerves
options.B: The appearance of the canal, eardrum color, landmark visibility, and any abnormal findings
options.C: The exact brand and serial number of the otoscope device used
options.D: Only the patient's reported hearing test scores from previous years

explanation: Good clinical notes always describe what you actually saw—like the color of the eardrum and whether landmarks were clear—so you can track the patient's healing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why do patients in areas with few clinics feel extra pressured to stay quiet?

options.A: They receive free private insurance coverage
options.B: They prefer substandard medical equipment
options.C: They have few alternative clinics to go to if they are mistreated
options.D: They are legally forbidden from speaking to nurses

explanation: You got it! When there's nowhere else to go for care, patients feel too dependent to risk upsetting the staff. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why are drug doses typically much smaller when given intrathecally compared to orally?

options.A: The liver breaks down the medicine much faster in the spinal cord
options.B: The stomach acid destroys most of the oral medication before absorption
options.C: The drug goes directly to the central nervous system without being filtered first
options.D: The blood-brain barrier absorbs most of the drug before it works

explanation: Delivering medication straight to the cerebrospinal fluid bypasses systemic circulation and barriers, requiring less drug to achieve the desired effect. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the main goal of surgery when treating a patient with a torn heart muscle?

options.A: Replacing the damaged heart with an artificial mechanical pump
options.B: Directly suturing the tear and relieving pressure in the pericardium
options.C: Removing the entire outer layer of the pericardial sac permanently
options.D: Tying off the coronary arteries to prevent further blood loss

explanation: The surgeon's priority is to stitch up the heart muscle tear and open the sac to drain trapped blood so the heart can beat freely again. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is an important final step after finishing an eye irrigation for a chemical burn?

options.A: Rechecking the tear pH to ensure it has returned to normal
options.B: Rinsing the patient's entire face with rubbing alcohol
options.C: Instructing the patient to avoid blinking for two hours
options.D: Applying a tight eye patch with heavy pressure tape

explanation: Checking the pH one last time confirms that all the harmful chemical has been fully neutralized and washed away. Great wrap-up! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is a common stereotype that can unfairly hurt female patients?

options.A: Having their physical strength constantly overestimated
options.B: Being labeled as overly emotional or exaggerating pain
options.C: Being discouraged from ever seeking medical help
options.D: Being assumed to always be the primary breadwinner

explanation: Exactly. Dismissing women's physical symptoms as 'just being emotional' is a dangerous trap we must avoid as nurses. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which two bacteria are the most common and serious causes of newborn eye infections?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli
options.B: Herpes simplex virus and Candida albicans
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Brilliant! These two bugs are usually passed from mother to baby and cause the toughest eye infections. Knowing them helps you stay alert in the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h2)

question: In a busy clinic, how does a multi-dose medication vial usually get contaminated?

options.A: Using a previously used needle or syringe to enter the vial
options.B: Cleaning the rubber stopper with alcohol before every puncture
options.C: Storing the medicine bottle inside a warm medication refrigerator
options.D: Failing to shake the suspension liquid before drawing a dose

explanation: That's right! If a needle has touched a patient, using it to enter a shared multi-dose vial contaminates the whole bottle for everyone else. Always use a fresh, sterile needle and syringe! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which workplace strategy shows that a hospital truly cares about long-term staff motivation?

options.A: Sponsoring specialty certifications and clear career ladders
options.B: Lowering entry-level salaries to save money for equipment
options.C: Reducing annual vacation days to increase bedside coverage
options.D: Eliminating all staff meetings to maximize shift hours

explanation: When a hospital helps you grow your skills and gives you clear paths to climb higher, you feel valued and ready to stay! [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h7)

question: How can a community health nurse best address local suspicion regarding health surveys?

options.A: Ignore the suspicious residents and only interview hospital staff
options.B: Collect data secretly at night without telling community members
options.C: Involve respected local leaders and explain the purpose clearly
options.D: Threaten residents with fines if they refuse to answer questions

explanation: Partnering with trusted community figures helps dispel myths and reassures residents that the health activities are safe and beneficial. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h8)

question: If a patient's hands have a fine, gentle tremble during a quick physical check, what might this point to?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Fluid overload
options.C: Hyperthyroidism
options.D: Adrenal suppression

explanation: When the thyroid is in overdrive (hyperthyroidism), it speeds up your metabolism and makes the nervous system super jittery, which often shows up as shaky hands. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h2)

question: In nursing, what does 'bundling care' mean when it comes to helping patients sleep?

options.A: Administering all daily medications at the exact same morning hour
options.B: Wrapping the patient tightly in heavy wool blankets
options.C: Grouping multiple care tasks together to reduce the number of times a patient is woken up
options.D: Sharing night shift duties evenly between nurses and assistants

explanation: Instead of waking your patient up every hour for a different task, you combine vital signs, meds, and dressings into one visit. That way, they get longer stretches of uninterrupted sleep! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h5)

question: When should a nurse recommend a deeper medical checkup beyond basic history-taking for menstrual pain?

options.A: When the patient is a teenager experiencing her very first periods
options.B: When mild cramping is relieved easily by simple rest and warmth
options.C: When there is a strong family history of normal menstruation
options.D: When secondary dysmenorrhoea or pelvic pathology is suspected

explanation: You nailed it! If standard relief doesn't work or pain starts later in life, we need to investigate deeper for conditions like endometriosis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the key sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It gets worse when the patient sits up and improves when lying flat
options.B: It feels like a sharp electrical shock running down both legs
options.C: It stays at the exact same intensity regardless of body position
options.D: It only occurs during the night and disappears by afternoon

explanation: You nailed it! Low fluid pressure pulls on pain-sensitive areas when upright, which eases up when the patient lies horizontal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h7)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: System, Balance, Assessment, Review
options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Activity, Rate
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Behavior, Assessment, Response

explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool that helps healthcare workers share critical patient information clearly and concisely during handovers. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h6)

question: How does a nurse act as a true advocate for an adolescent patient?

options.A: By reporting every minor detail of counseling sessions to village elders
options.B: By charging extra fees for confidential consultations
options.C: By restricting access to health information to adults only
options.D: By protecting client confidentiality and defending their right to respectful care

explanation: You got it! As an advocate, you stand up for your young patients' rights to safe, private, and judgment-free care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h6)

question: What is the medical term for the very first menstrual period in a young female?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Menarche
options.C: Menopause
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Menarche is the term used to describe the onset of the first menstrual cycle during puberty. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h1)

question: A community nurse notices that pregnant women in a remote village have nowhere to go for antenatal care. What is the best action?

options.A: Tell the pregnant women to relocate permanently to the capital
options.B: Ignore the issue since hospitals are solely a government duty
options.C: Collaborate with a voluntary health agency to set up mobile clinics
options.D: Wait until the villagers independently build a standard hospital

explanation: Brilliant nursing judgment! Partnering with voluntary organizations is one of the smartest ways to bring care straight to underserved communities. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h8)

question: What can happen if a nurse rudely dismisses a patient for using traditional local remedies?

options.A: The hospital will automatically discharge the patient for misconduct
options.B: Local herbalists will protest outside the hospital gates
options.C: The patient will instantly abandon all traditional beliefs forever
options.D: The patient may hide information or delay seeking crucial medical help

explanation: Spot on. Harsh judgments push patients away, making them hide vital health info or avoid getting help when they need it most. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is a common trap nurses must avoid when assessing oncology patients?

options.A: Relying too much on lab results instead of talking to the patient
options.B: Dismissing subtle confusion or fatigue as normal chemotherapy side effects
options.C: Measuring fluid intake and output when the patient is stable
options.D: Checking vital signs too often during a night shift

explanation: Subtle mental status changes can be the first clue of a serious metabolic or structural emergency, not just everyday treatment fatigue. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which tiny, hair-like parts of the respiratory tract get paralyzed and destroyed by cigarette smoke?

options.A: Cilia
options.B: Alveoli
options.C: Bronchioles
options.D: Pleura

explanation: Cilia are the tiny sweeping brushes of the lungs that clear out mucus and dirt. Smoke damages them badly, but understanding this puts you one step ahead! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of "value clarification" workshops for nursing staff?

options.A: To train nurses on advanced surgical procedures like abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: To enforce strict legal penalties against patients who induce abortions
options.C: To help nurses set aside personal biases to provide non-judgmental care
options.D: To update hospital billing policies for emergency obstetric services

explanation: We all have personal beliefs, but value clarification helps us check our biases at the door so we can treat every single patient with professional, loving kindness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h5)

question: What is the ultimate aim of a community health nurse in mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity so the community runs its own health programs
options.B: Collecting data to publish research papers in medical journals
options.C: Making sure the local clinic receives a large budget from abroad
options.D: Ensuring the nurse becomes the most respected person in the village

explanation: The goal of community mobilisation is self-reliance, where locals have the skills to manage their health without constant outside intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: Which blood vessels carry used, deoxygenated blood away from the baby back to the placenta?

options.A: Pulmonary veins
options.B: Carotid arteries
options.C: Umbilical veins
options.D: Umbilical arteries

explanation: You've got this! Two umbilical arteries take the baby's waste products and deoxygenated blood right back to the placenta to be cleaned by the mother's system. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: Why can diagnosing Pick's disease be tricky in the beginning?

options.A: Its behavioral symptoms can be mistaken for psychiatric disorders.
options.B: Standard MRI scanners cannot image the frontal lobes clearly.
options.C: Routine blood tests can easily confuse it with normal aging.
options.D: Patients usually retain perfect memory until the final days.

explanation: Because the very first signs are personality changes and apathy, doctors sometimes mistake it for depression, anxiety, or mental health issues rather than a brain disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h4)

question: How do migrating cancer cells manage to break into nearby blood vessels?

options.A: They secrete enzymes that break down surrounding tissue barriers
options.B: They attract white blood cells to carry them into circulation
options.C: They wait for the blood vessel walls to rupture from high pressure
options.D: They shrink in size until they slip through normal cell walls

explanation: Spot on! Cancer cells release special chemical enzymes that chew through tissue barriers and blood vessel walls, letting them slip right into circulation. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T2#GNS321_U1_T2_h6)

question: What happens to the blood vessels in the skin when the body needs to cool down?

options.A: They widen to bring warm blood closer to the skin surface
options.B: They thicken their walls to prevent any fluid loss
options.C: They stop carrying blood entirely to save energy
options.D: They narrow to trap heat deep inside the body core

explanation: You got it! Widening these vessels (vasodilation) lets extra body heat escape easily into the cooler air outside. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h4)

question: How is spongy bone different from compact bone?

options.A: It lacks a blood supply entirely
options.B: It is made completely of soft cartilage
options.C: It is found only on the outer surface of long bones
options.D: It has a porous, web-like structure instead of solid layers

explanation: Spot on! Spongy bone looks a bit like a honeycomb with little struts (trabeculae), making it lightweight, while compact bone is super solid and dense. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h2)

question: How many days of backup contraception are needed when starting oral contraceptives in the middle of a cycle?

options.A: One day
options.B: Seven days
options.C: Thirty days
options.D: Fourteen days

explanation: It takes 7 full days of taking the pill consistently to reliably stop ovulation if you don't start on day one of your period. Remind your clients to use a condom during that first week! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h5)

question: When measuring fluid from a drainage container, how should the nurse read the volume accurately?

options.A: By guessing the amount based on how full the bulb looks
options.B: By weighing the container on a bathroom scale while wet
options.C: By holding the container high up near the ceiling lights
options.D: At eye level with the liquid resting on a flat surface

explanation: Reading fluid levels at eye level on a flat surface prevents parallax errors and ensures the measurement recorded on the chart is correct. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which of the following is a clear contraindication for nasogastric tube insertion?

options.A: Mild nausea from a viral infection
options.B: Uncomplicated type 2 diabetes
options.C: Severe facial and nasal fractures
options.D: A history of high blood pressure

explanation: Passing a tube through broken facial bones can push the tube into the cranial vault instead of the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why are nurse managers usually involved in management audits?

options.A: To connect executive policies with actual bedside practices
options.B: To write new financial accounting laws for the ministry of health
options.C: To punish staff members who make clinical documentation errors
options.D: To replace the hospital chief executive officer during emergencies

explanation: Nurse managers are the amazing bridge between big hospital bosses and everyday patient care. Their input helps auditors see how administrative choices truly play out on the ward! [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h1)

question: Why is the immune system so important for our survival?

options.A: It regulates the normal daily temperature of the human body
options.B: It digests food nutrients inside the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: It controls the production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.D: It protects the body against harmful microorganisms in the environment

explanation: Spot on! Think of your immune system as your body's personal security guard, constantly working behind the scenes to shield you from harmful germs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which medical term means a dangerously low platelet count that makes a patient bleed more easily?

options.A: Thrombocytopenia
options.B: Leukopenia
options.C: Polycythemia
options.D: Erythrocytosis

explanation: Break the word down: 'thrombo' relates to clotting, 'cyten' means cells, and 'penia' means too little. So thrombocytopenia simply means a low number of clotting cells (platelets)! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why do public health campaigns often focus mass deworming programs on school-aged children?

options.A: Children have the highest worm burdens and engage in behaviors that spread eggs
options.B: Adults are completely immune to reinfection after adolescence
options.C: Deworming tablets are only approved by regulators for pediatric use
options.D: Children are the only population that can develop lung complications

explanation: Kids play outside in the soil and tend to carry the highest number of worms, making school deworming programs super effective. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T22#GNS313_U2_T22_h6)

question: How does poverty directly affect a pregnant woman's health outcomes?

options.A: It forces healthcare providers to deny them basic vaccinations
options.B: It completely stops the placenta from producing progesterone and estrogen
options.C: It restricts their ability to afford transport and hospital fees during emergencies
options.D: It guarantees that they will develop gestational diabetes late in the third trimester

explanation: Financial barriers can prevent women from reaching skilled medical facilities when urgent complications arise. It's a reminder of why accessible healthcare is so vital. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical practice when presenting qualitative research results?

options.A: Revealing the real names of participants to give them credit
options.B: Reporting all findings honestly, even unexpected ones
options.C: Separating factual results from personal opinions
options.D: Using pseudonyms to protect participant confidentiality

explanation: Participant confidentiality is paramount; revealing real names without explicit consent breaches ethical research standards. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a survivorship care plan?

options.A: To manage acute surgical complications in the hospital
options.B: To replace the need for any further primary care visits
options.C: To guarantee that cancer will never return in the future
options.D: To outline treatment history and schedule ongoing surveillance

explanation: Think of it as a roadmap. A survivorship plan summarizes past treatments and maps out future health check-ups. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h9)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason to call a Rapid Response Team?

options.A: A sudden drop in oxygen saturation
options.B: Unexplained chest pain or pressure
options.C: A patient complaining of mild boredom
options.D: A sudden decrease in mental alertness

explanation: You've got this! Feeling bored is uncomfortable, but it isn't an emergency. Oxygen drops, chest pain, and sudden confusion, however, are major warning signs that need immediate backup! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why are patients told to avoid signing important legal documents for 24 hours after a sedated endoscopy?

options.A: Hospitals are legally liable for outside contracts signed.
options.B: Sedative drugs can temporarily impair judgment and memory.
options.C: The bright lights in the procedure room damage eye muscles.
options.D: Anesthesia causes permanent changes in logical thinking.

explanation: Even if they feel completely awake, leftover sedation affects clear thinking and memory, so making major choices can wait until the next day. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h8)

question: During a CT scan with contrast, a patient suddenly develops widespread hives, facial swelling, and mild wheezing. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Ask the patient to hold their breath until the scanning is finished.
options.B: Stop the contrast injection and notify the medical team immediately.
options.C: Reassure the patient that hives are a completely normal side effect.
options.D: Administer a dose of oral pain medication to calm the patient.

explanation: Hives and wheezing indicate an allergic reaction to the contrast media, requiring the immediate cessation of the infusion and prompt emergency medical intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which serious condition is a major maternal complication directly linked to severe, uncontrolled blood loss?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: Massive blood loss rapidly reduces circulating blood volume, leading directly to hypovolemic shock if not treated aggressively. Keep up the steady pace! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h7)

question: What happens when the sleep-promoting centers quiet down the reticular activating system?

options.A: Metabolic rate spikes rapidly
options.B: Voluntary muscle tone becomes rigid
options.C: The brain transitions into sleep
options.D: Sensory awareness dramatically increases

explanation: When those wake-up signals from the reticular activating system quiet down, your brain is finally able to drift off to sleep. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h2)

question: A patient suddenly loses their voice and sounds very hoarse after a cold. Which part of the airway is likely inflamed?

options.A: The palatine tonsils
options.B: The nasal cavity
options.C: The larynx
options.D: The frontal sinuses

explanation: Well done! The larynx is your voice box, so when it gets inflamed (laryngitis), your vocal cords swell and your voice gets raspy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why is it super important for nurses to know the generic name of a drug?

options.A: It is the only name recognized by hospital billing departments
options.B: It remains universal and prevents confusion across different manufacturing companies
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact physical shape and color of the pill

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping fast and calls the doctor using SBAR. What should go into the 'Recommendation' part?

question: Which of these is an early warning sign that conflict is brewing on a ward?

question: What is the age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

question: Why do lung problems often affect the rest of the body?

options.A: Lung infections spread directly to the brain within hours

options.D: The heart stops pumping blood when the lungs become inflamed

question: Why does the nurse occasionally tap the side of the medication cup during the procedure?

options.C: To signal to the patient that the treatment session is halfway finished

question: A nurse is caring for a patient admitted with a highly contagious airborne respiratory infection. Which precaution is NOT appropriate for this specific case?

options.A: Housing the patient inside a negative pressure isolation room
options.B: Placing the patient in a standard open ward bed with no barriers
options.C: Ensuring healthcare workers wear fitted N95 respirator masks
options.D: Limiting visitor access to protect other vulnerable patients

explanation: Airborne infections require negative pressure rooms and specialized masks, not open wards where droplet nuclei can easily infect others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why shouldn't nurse educators rely on just one single learning theory?

options.A: Students will complain if they only experience one teaching style
options.B: Different nursing skills and learning goals require different theoretical approaches
options.C: Accreditation bodies legally require schools to use all five theories
options.D: Only one theory has ever been scientifically proven to work

question: What is the main purpose of a vagus nerve stimulation device in epilepsy care?

options.A: To permanently cure the structural brain scar
options.B: To completely stop all electrical activity in the brain
options.C: To replace the function of damaged temporal lobe tissue
options.D: To reduce how often and how severe seizures occur

explanation: Think of a vagus nerve stimulator as a gentle pacemaker for the brain that helps dial down the frequency and intensity of seizures when drugs aren't enough. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h6)

question: Why must even experienced registered nurses take part in continuous professional development?

options.A: Experienced nurses tend to forget all basic nursing procedures
options.B: Medical knowledge and clinical techniques continuously evolve over time
options.C: Hospital accreditation boards punish facilities that do not hold daily exams
options.D: New nursing graduates require constant supervision from senior colleagues

question: What is the primary intervention for a patient after receiving a CT scan with intravenous contrast?

question: What's the main difference between a regular fever and hyperthermia?

options.A: Hyperthermia responds to antipyretic drugs, while fever never does.
options.B: Fever only occurs in children, while hyperthermia only occurs in adults.
options.C: Fever involves the brain raising its temperature target, while hyperthermia is a failure to cool down.
options.D: Hyperthermia is caused by infections, while fever is caused by weather.

explanation: Think of it this way: a fever happens because your brain's thermostat is intentionally turned up (like fighting an infection). Hyperthermia happens when the body is overwhelmed by heat and can't cool itself down, and normal fever meds won't fix that thermostat setting! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do midwives and nurses group pregnancy signs into presumptive, probable, and positive categories?

options.A: To separate normal hormonal shifts from pathological illnesses

options.C: To structure physical assessments and guide further testing logically
options.D: To determine the exact gender of the developing fetus early on

question: Why is that long plateau phase so important for the heart?

options.A: It speeds up the heart rate during periods of heavy physical exercise
options.B: It prevents the heart muscle from ever experiencing fatigue
options.C: It allows the pacemaker cells to reset their baseline electrical charge
options.D: It gives the heart enough time to fully squeeze blood out of its chambers

explanation: The plateau keeps the contraction going just long enough to push blood completely out into your body instead of just a quick twitch. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which food group gives you a double blessing of both plant protein and complex carbohydrates?

options.A: Pure vegetable oils

question: A mum's partograph has crossed past the action line. What is your best next step?

options.A: Wait another four hours to see if labour picks up speed on its own.
options.B: Initiate definitive medical or surgical interventions immediately.
options.C: Stop monitoring vital signs to reduce patient anxiety.
options.D: Discharge the patient home since labour is progressing slowly.

question: Why are professional boundaries so important in nursing?

options.B: They ensure the nurse never has to show empathy to anyone

question: What does the first menstrual period (menarche) mainly tell us about a young girl?

options.D: Complete closure of the pelvic growth plates

question: Why do patients with leprosy often get burns or cuts on their hands and feet without realizing it?

options.A: Circulatory failure prevents blood flow to the fingers and toes.

options.C: The pathogen directly causes bones in the digits to dissolve.
options.D: Bacteria destroy sensory nerve fibers, causing local anesthesia.

question: A patient arrives pale, dizzy, and bleeding heavily after an unsafe abortion. What action should you take right away?

options.C: Ask the patient to write down a detailed confession of the act

question: Why are community referrals and health linkages important in post-abortion care?

options.A: They replace the need for emergency treatment during complications

options.C: They support long-term wellness and prevent future reproductive health issues

question: When giving nursing care after an abortion, what does a holistic approach mainly mean?

options.A: Recognizing overlapping systemic illnesses
options.B: Treating only physical symptoms
options.C: Focusing solely on uterine health
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent cross-contamination in the fridge?

question: What physical pressure change forces the foramen ovale to snap shut when a baby is born?

question: Besides severe dizziness, what other symptoms often point toward Meniere's disease?

question: What does the Drug Control Act primarily regulate?

question: What does a sudden, significant drop in the baby's heart rate during a contraction usually suggest?

question: What is a common misconception regarding family planning services in many communities?

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four central concepts in the nursing metaparadigm?

question: What is a recommended nursing intervention to help prevent post-dural puncture headaches?

question: What is a common cultural view in some Nigerian communities that affects family planning?

question: What happens if you use a single-dose medication vial for more than one patient?

question: A patient asks if she can get pregnant before her first period returns after an abortion. What should you tell her?

question: A pregnant patient comes to the clinic vomiting ten times a day, unable to keep water down, and showing ketones in her urine. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.B: Gestational hypertension

question: What is the main feature that separates stable angina from unstable angina?

question: When must you wear a surgical mask while working in the surgical suite?

question: Finding protein in someone's routine urine test most often points to an issue with what?

question: What is the main difference between good (appropriate) polypharmacy and bad (problematic) polypharmacy?

question: What do we call it when an older adult takes several different medications at the same time?

question: How should a nurse best respond to a community member expressing fear that birth control causes illness?

question: Which type of small intestinal disorder involves long-term, deep inflammation of the bowel wall that can form strictures and fistulae?

question: How do azole antifungal drugs stop fungi from growing?

question: What is a fecal impaction?

question: Where do T-lymphocytes go to mature?

question: Which group of medications is well-known for causing sexual side effects like low libido or delayed orgasm?

question: Why is teaching patients how to avoid environmental hazards so important after an insect sting recovery?

question: Why is it clinically important to know that testicular lymph drains to lumbar nodes while scrotal lymph drains to inguinal nodes?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a positive feedback loop?

options.B: Cortisol suppressing the hypothalamus from releasing stress hormones

question: Which two major legal codes deal with criminal law across Nigeria?

question: Why is the primary survey performed in a strict ABCDE order?

question: Why do ICUs often pause a patient's sedative medications for a short time every day?

question: A young student in Nigeria worries that taking Postinor-2 will make her barren. How should you respond?

options.B: Scold her for engaging in premarital sex and refuse to give her the medication

question: What type of joints hold the flat bones of the skull tightly together so they don't move?

question: What are the three core things the TNM staging system looks at?

question: Which of these is NOT an infection prevention item found in a midwifery kit?

question: What do we mean by patient harm in a clinical setting?

question: Why do nurses always warn patients with bleeding problems to stay away from everyday painkillers like ibuprofen?

options.B: NSAIDs instantly destroy all stored vitamin K reserves located inside the liver

question: How do antiviral medications help male patients who have genital herpes?

question: How do nurses directly help with cancer epidemiology in clinical and community settings?

question: What is the main goal of teamwork between government health structures and NGOs?

question: What is dumping syndrome?

question: Why do we need multiple organizations teaming up to prevent unsafe abortions?

question: At what point in an illness can a patient usually start receiving palliative care?

question: Which imaging tool is considered the gold standard for mapping complex reproductive tract birth defects?

question: Why do droplet precautions only require a standard mask within a short distance of the patient?

question: Which specific medication is used to treat encephalitis caused by the herpes simplex virus?

question: Who are key partners for nurses when organizing grassroots advocacy against child marriage in rural communities?

question: What is the primary output of the action planning phase?

question: As a nurse, why is the subcutaneous layer (hypodermis) often chosen for giving certain injections?

question: What do we mean when we talk about a person's caloric intake?

question: What is the main role of the water seal chamber in a chest drainage unit?

question: Why do home health nurses need to watch out for non-physical abuse just as much?

question: Why do we usually need to treat everyone in a household if just one person has pinworms?

question: Which type of mental ability actually tends to stay stable or even improve as people grow older?

question: What is the purpose of the clean apron inside the home visiting kit?

question: Where are the internal female reproductive organs primarily located?

question: How do essential amino acids mostly move across the placental membrane into the fetal blood?

question: At what Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score do doctors usually decide to insert an artificial airway (intubation) to protect the patient?

question: How do seizure medications that block sodium channels actually work?

question: Why is it helpful for student nurses to understand research paradigms?

question: Why might a surgeon sometimes create a temporary diverting colostomy during a fistula repair?

question: What does 'coffee-ground emesis' (vomit that looks like coffee grounds) usually tell you during an assessment?

question: Why shouldn't you rush or speed too much when transporting an accident victim?

options.D: Assessment
